column1: Most decks start from a blank slide. You draw boxes, line them up, nudge them again, and the message gets lost along the way. Here you decide the message first, and the layout follows from it.
Decide the message first; the layout follows.
This is Spec-Driven Presentation Maker. You decide what to say; AI builds how to show it, and you can watch every slide being assembled, region by region.
Decide what to say.\n{{#EEF0F4:AI builds how to show it.}}
When a slide needs changing, point at it. Draw a frame around the part, write what should change, and send all your frames together as one request. Each comment is handled on the slide it points at.
Draw frames, comment, send them as one request.
Try it in one command. Then ask your AI agent for slides, run sdpm webui to work in the browser, or deploy it on AWS for your team. The full install line is in the README.
Then ask your AI agent, run {{font=Menlo,#EEF0F4:sdpm webui}}, or deploy on AWS.
Building happens in two passes. First, one pass draws the frame and the regions of every slide, so the whole deck shares one design. Then several AI agents work at once, each filling its own slides.
{{bold:Then every slide is built at once}}
First the frame for every slide, then several AI agents fill them at once.
Before a single slide exists, you agree on three short documents, in this order: the brief, the style and the outline. You approve each one before the next.
Who it is for, what\nthey should do
You approve each one before the next.
The same spec becomes either kind of deck. Build a PowerPoint file on your own template that you can keep editing, or a single HTML file with interactive slides that runs in any browser.
An editable PowerPoint file, or an interactive HTML deck.
